epics.title: codebase consistency sweep
epics.description: Fix formatting violations and consolidate structural duplication identified in the May 2026 consistency analysis.
epics.notes: Findings from rt analyze list-smells + find-duplicates sweep on 2026-05-11.

epics.title: SOLID Adherence Analysis
epics.description: Family of rt analyze solid subcommands that detect likely SOLID-principle violations using Roslyn semantic model. One detector per principle; output is JSON grouped by detector name.
epics.notes: P2. Five child stories: SRP, ISP, DIP, OCP, LSP. Each independently shippable.

epics.title: Add structured JSON output to all inspect/analyze commands
epics.description: All rt inspect and rt analyze commands should support --json output so automation consumers (agents, scripts, CI tools) can pipe results without text parsing. Eight commands currently output plain text only.
epics.notes: P2. Affects: find-refs, find-callers, find-undocumented, find-unused, circular-deps, find-magic-strings, list-imports, list-smells. Template: see describe/outline/find-impl which already have JSON output.

epics.title: Platform abstractions: IWorkspaceSessionFactory + ISolutionApplier
epics.description: Introduce injectable abstractions for WorkspaceLoader and SolutionWriter so commands depend on interfaces, not static helpers. Enables testability without AsyncLocal overrides and unblocks daemon workspace caching. Must be a single coordinated change across all ~30 commands.
epics.notes: P2. Architecture gate NoStaticWorkspaceLoaderUse already exists in tests/. rt-006 + rt-007 from issues backlog. Must ship together — splitting doubles the 30-command churn.

epics.title: Consistent command contracts and migration ratchets
epics.description: Make rt commands consistent across handler structure, option vocabulary, metadata, output envelopes, and symbol resolution so dogfooding workflows are predictable and architecture tests can ratchet progress.
epics.notes: From rt dogfooding consistency discussion on 2026-05-15.

userStories.title: rt: convert-static-class — fix field and ctor formatting in existing-constructor path
userStories.description: When a consumer class already has constructors, AddConstructorInjection inserts the new field without a trailing newline, causing it to merge with the existing first member on the same line. Similarly, AddConstructorParameter inserts parameters without comma spacing and prepends assignments without newlines before the closing brace. dotnet format corrects these cosmetically but they should be emitted correctly. Discovered during US-027 df dry-run.
acceptanceCriteria: When a consumer class already has a constructor, the injected field is inserted on its own line (with correct indentation), not concatenated with the existing first member on the same line
When AddConstructorParameter adds a parameter to an existing constructor, a space follows the preceding comma in the parameter list
When AddConstructorParameter prepends an assignment to the constructor body, the assignment is on its own line before the closing brace
All three fixes apply when multiple constructors are present in the consumer class
Existing tests for add_dependencies_to_existing_instance_constructors remain green
userStories.urgencyReason: convert-static-class — field/ctor formatting. Smallest of the trio so floats above US-037/038 inside the band.
userStories.notes: P2. df dogfood bug. Sibling of the no-constructor formatting bug fixed in the df/convert-static-class-interface-and-di branch commit 1fcf269.

userStories.title: Introduce IWorkspaceSessionFactory + WorkspaceSession (rt-006)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want all commands to depend on IWorkspaceSessionFactory instead of the concrete WorkspaceLoader type so that the static coupling is broken and daemon workspace caching becomes possible.
acceptanceCriteria: IWorkspaceSessionFactory interface defined in src/RoslynTools/Core/ with GetSolutionAsync(string?) and LoadWorkspaceAsync(string?) signatures matching the existing WorkspaceLoader instance methods
WorkspaceLoader implements IWorkspaceSessionFactory (no new WorkspaceSession class required — the existing instance-API WorkspaceLoader fills that role)
IWorkspaceSessionFactory registered in Bootstrap.cs alongside the WorkspaceLoader singleton

All 57 production call sites depend on IWorkspaceSessionFactory, not the concrete WorkspaceLoader type (covers src/RoslynTools.Cli/Commands/, src/RoslynTools/Services/, src/RoslynTools/Core/, and MCP handlers)
rt inspect find-refs --symbol WorkspaceLoader --solution RoslynTools.slnx shows only the type-declaration and test-fixture references (no production call sites)
Architecture gate NoStaticWorkspaceLoaderUse strengthened to also flag concrete WorkspaceLoader references from src/ outside the class itself, and continues to pass
Static WorkspaceLoader.LoadAsync compat surface deleted (the gate proves it has no production callers)
WorkspaceLoader.UseOverride test-hook reworked to stub IWorkspaceSessionFactory; existing tests pass without changes to call sites
Must ship in same PR as US-054 — partial rollout is not safe
userStories.urgencyReason: EP-008: IWorkspaceSessionFactory. Must ship together with US-054 — splitting doubles the 57-site churn (per epic notes). Heaviest items → bottom of band.
userStories.notes: P2. Existing foundation (instance-API WorkspaceLoader, DI registration, AsyncLocal Override, passing NoStaticWorkspaceLoaderUse gate) reduces remaining work from a full re-architecture to an interface-extraction + type-reference migration. Real blast radius: 57 production call sites (45 LoadWorkspaceAsync + 12 GetSolutionAsync) and 27 test files. From issue rt-006.
userStories.resolution: Shipped on branch ep-008-isessionfactory. IWorkspaceSessionFactory interface introduced (Core/IWorkspaceSessionFactory.cs) with GetSolutionAsync + LoadWorkspaceAsync + static CreateDefault factory. WorkspaceLoader implements it. RtServiceProvider gained GetOrDefault<T>(Func<T>) for interface-typed resolution with test-friendly fallback. All ~57 production call sites migrated (11 inspect fallback + 45 RtServiceProvider sites + 2 MCP handlers). NoConcreteWorkspaceLoaderInProduction architecture gate added and passing — production refs limited to WorkspaceLoader.cs, IWorkspaceSessionFactory.cs, and Bootstrap.cs (composition root). Static WorkspaceLoader.LoadAsync retained as test-only convenience (per advisor) with updated docstring; existing NoStaticWorkspaceLoaderUse gate keeps it out of src/. 1145 tests pass.

userStories.title: Migrate direct SolutionWriter call sites to ISolutionChangeWriter (rt-007)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want all production code that mutates a solution to depend on ISolutionChangeWriter instead of calling the static SolutionWriter.ApplyChangesAsync directly, so that mutation tests can stub the writer and daemon caching doesn't fight per-call workspace ownership. Bundled with US-053 so the related command churn ships once.
acceptanceCriteria: ISolutionChangeWriter interface (already defined in src/RoslynTools/Services/SolutionChangeWriter.cs with Task ApplyChangesAsync(Solution, Solution, bool dryRun)) is the sole production path to SolutionWriter — the existing name is kept; renaming to ISolutionApplier is out of scope

5 direct SolutionWriter.ApplyChangesAsync call sites migrated to ISolutionChangeWriter via DI: src/RoslynTools/Core/ConsoleLoggingCore.cs:76, src/RoslynTools.Cli/CommandHandlers/ChangeSignatureCommandHandlers.cs (lines 32, 62, 94, 126), src/RoslynTools.Cli/Commands/ConvertConsoleLoggingCommand.cs:194, src/RoslynTools.Cli/Commands/ExtractMethodCommand.cs:112

New architecture gate NoDirectSolutionWriterUse added under tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Architecture/, mirroring NoStaticWorkspaceLoaderUse, banning direct SolutionWriter.ApplyChangesAsync calls from src/ outside the SolutionChangeWriter adapter
AsyncLocal Override pattern added to ISolutionChangeWriter so mutation tests can capture writes without disk I/O (matches WorkspaceLoader.UseOverride ergonomics)
rt inspect find-refs --symbol SolutionWriter --solution RoslynTools.slnx shows only the SolutionChangeWriter adapter and SolutionWriter's own type-declaration locations after the change
All existing tests pass
Implemented in the same PR as US-053
userStories.urgencyReason: EP-008: ISolutionChangeWriter coverage. Pair with US-053.
userStories.notes: P2. ISolutionChangeWriter + SolutionChangeWriter adapter already exist (src/RoslynTools/Services/SolutionChangeWriter.cs) and are DI-registered. Real blast radius: 5 direct call sites (much smaller than the original '22 fan-in' estimate, because the adapter already siphons most callers). From issue rt-007.
userStories.resolution: Shipped on branch ep-008-isessionfactory. Migrated 7 direct SolutionWriter.ApplyChangesAsync call sites (ConsoleLoggingCore, ChangeSignatureCommandHandlers x4, ConvertConsoleLoggingCommand, ExtractMethodCommand) to RtServiceProvider.GetOrDefault(ISolutionChangeWriter.CreateDefault).ApplyChangesAsync. ISolutionChangeWriter + SolutionChangeWriter moved from RoslynTools.Services into RoslynTools.Core to break a Core→Services→Core cycle that emerged when ConsoleLoggingCore needed the interface. Added static ISolutionChangeWriter.CreateDefault() factory mirroring IWorkspaceSessionFactory. NoDirectSolutionWriterUse architecture gate added and passing — production refs to SolutionWriter limited to SolutionChangeWriter adapter only. 1145 tests pass.

userStories.title: rt dump-help --json: emit machine-readable command catalog
userStories.description: As an LLM agent, I want `rt dump-help --json` to emit the full RtCommandInfo catalog as structured JSON so I can ingest the command surface programmatically instead of parsing prose.
acceptanceCriteria: `rt dump-help --json` exits 0 and writes valid JSON to stdout.
The JSON document includes every command discovered by the reflection-based registry — the command count equals what plain `rt dump-help` reports.

Each command entry includes Name, Category, Mutates, JsonOutput, Aliases, WhenToUse, Examples, KnownIssues, and SupportedFormats from RtCommandInfo. Missing or null fields are represented explicitly (no silent drops).
The plain `rt dump-help` (no flag) text output is byte-identical to today's — JSON is purely additive.
An LLM can parse the JSON output and reconstruct the command surface without reading any source file or markdown.
If `--strict-json` is passed alongside, the output is RFC 8259 compliant (non-ASCII escaped as \uXXXX).
userStories.urgencyReason: rt dump-help --json — unlocks agent automation; touches one command. Opens the EP-007 wave.
userStories.notes: P2. Deferred from LLM-ergonomics quick-wins plan. The RtCommandInfo record and reflection-discovered registry in App.cs already expose every field — wiring it through JsonRenderer should be near-free. Affected files: src/RoslynTools.Cli/Commands/DumpHelpCommand.cs, src/RoslynTools/Core/RtCommandInfo.cs.

userStories.title: Expand command help text with output shape, exit codes, and error modes
userStories.description: As an LLM agent, I want every rt command's --help to describe its output shape, exit codes, and common error modes so I can predict behaviour without source-diving or trial-and-error.
acceptanceCriteria: Every command's `--help` output includes a section stating the output format (text vs JSON vs both, mutating vs read-only).
Every command's `--help` lists the exit codes it can return (0, 1, 2) and the trigger for each (success / error / decisions required).
Every command's `--help` lists at least one common error mode the user should expect (e.g. "symbol not found", "ambiguous match without --decisions", "file outside solution").
Information is sourced from RtCommandInfo (or a new metadata field on it) rather than hand-maintained in each Command.cs — no drift between help and reality.
`docs/COMMANDS.md` regenerates on build and includes the new fields for every command.
An LLM reading only `rt <cmd> --help` can predict the shape of stdout, stderr, and exit code for both success and the most common failure.
userStories.urgencyReason: Expand command help text with output shape + exit codes. Smallest of the discoverability wave — floats first.
userStories.notes: P2. Deferred from LLM-ergonomics quick-wins plan. Sampled commands (DescribeCommand, FindCallersCommand, ExtractMethodCommand) currently have one-line descriptions only — no failure mode docs, no output schema. Drive from RtCommandInfo so docs/COMMANDS.md stays in sync.

userStories.title: Make --decisions YAML schema self-discoverable from the CLI
userStories.description: As an LLM agent, I want the --decisions YAML schema to be discoverable from rt --help (or a meta sub-command) so I can author a decisions file without reading DecisionStore.cs source.
acceptanceCriteria: `rt --help` (or a sub-command such as `rt decisions --schema`) prints the YAML schema for the --decisions file.
The printed schema documents every field used today (id, q, options, choose) with types and a one-line description per field.
A complete worked example is included: the YAML rt would write on first run, plus the same YAML with `choose:` filled in by the user.
An LLM that has not read source can author or edit a --decisions YAML correctly using only CLI help output.
When --decisions YAML fails to parse or is missing a required field, stderr reports which file and which entry (id) is malformed — not a stack trace.
Existing --decisions behaviour (exit 2, write pending entries) is unchanged.
userStories.urgencyReason: Self-describing --decisions YAML schema.
userStories.notes: P3. Deferred from LLM-ergonomics quick-wins plan. The mechanism is mentioned in --help but the file structure (fields, indices, how to fill the choose field) requires source inspection today. Affected files: src/RoslynTools/Core/Decisions/DecisionStore.cs, src/RoslynTools/Core/Decisions/DecisionEntry.cs, src/RoslynTools.Cli/App.cs.

userStories.title: Finish stderr discipline migration: Console.Write to RtLog/RtConsole
userStories.description: As an LLM agent piping stdout to a parser and stderr to logs, I want every rt command to honour the stdout=results, stderr=diagnostics contract so I can rely on stream separation without per-command quirks.
acceptanceCriteria: No remaining `Console.Write*` calls exist in src/RoslynTools/Commands/ or src/RoslynTools.Cli/Commands/ (verified by grep, gated in CI or a unit test).
All progress and diagnostic messages from command handlers route through RtLog.* (stderr).
All primary command results route through RtConsole.Write (stdout).
Existing tests pass without modification (output contracts preserved).
docs/logging-standards.md is updated to remove the "migration incomplete" notice and document the now-enforced convention.
An LLM piping stdout to a JSON parser and stderr to logs gets clean separation across every command.
userStories.urgencyReason: Finish stderr discipline migration: stray Console.Write to stdout in error paths. Completes a longstanding push.
userStories.notes: P2. Deferred from LLM-ergonomics quick-wins plan. docs/logging-standards.md acknowledges the migration is in progress; several commands still call Console.Write directly. Maintenance work — does not change LLM behaviour at runtime today, but eliminates a future regression vector.

userStories.title: rt refactor extract-interface produces malformed output for internal classes
userStories.description: As a roslyn-tools developer, I want extract-interface to honor source class accessibility, include internal members when the source is internal, and emit syntactically valid C# so that I can dogfood it during DI migrations on internal types.
acceptanceCriteria: rt refactor extract-interface --type WorkspaceLoader --solution RoslynTools.slnx --dry-run emits a syntactically valid diff: the new interface name is inserted into the existing base list with proper formatting (space after comma, brace placement matching the file's brace style), and the resulting file would compile
Extracting from an internal sealed class produces an internal interface (not public). Accessibility of the generated interface matches the source class accessibility

Extracting from an internal class includes the class's internal members in the generated interface (today only public members are picked up). Public-only behaviour remains the default for public source classes

Regression test added covering an internal class with internal members and an existing IDisposable base list, asserting both the file compiles and the interface accessibility/membership matches expectation
rt refactor extract-interface --type WorkspaceLoader --solution RoslynTools.slnx (no dry-run) succeeds without producing files that fail dotnet build
userStories.notes: P2. Surfaced during EP-008/US-053 dogfood at branch ep-008-isessionfactory. Three bundled defects: (1) base-list insertion is malformed -- 'IDisposable\n,IWorkspaceLoader{' (no space, brace adjacent); (2) generated interface is hardcoded public regardless of source class accessibility (internal sealed class WorkspaceLoader yielded public interface IWorkspaceLoader); (3) only public members are extracted, missing internal GetSolutionAsync/LoadWorkspaceAsync from WorkspaceLoader. Repro: rt refactor extract-interface --type WorkspaceLoader --solution RoslynTools.slnx --dry-run. Forced fallback to hand-authoring IWorkspaceSessionFactory.

userStories.title: Eliminate RtServiceProvider.Get<T> service locator in favour of ctor injection
userStories.description: As a roslyn-tools developer, I want commands to depend on services via constructor injection so the ambient service-locator anti-pattern (RtServiceProvider.Get<T>()) disappears and command dependencies become explicit and testable.
acceptanceCriteria: IRtCommand contract revised to support instance classes — each command class is constructed by the DI container with required services injected via the constructor; the static Build() pattern is replaced with an instance Build() that closes over the injected services
App.Discover (or its replacement) resolves each command via the service provider rather than calling a static factory

All ~50 commands under src/RoslynTools.Cli/Commands/ (and src/RoslynTools.Cli/CommandHandlers/) refactored to declare their service dependencies as constructor parameters and reference them via private readonly fields
All 64 RtServiceProvider.Get<T>() and RtServiceProvider.GetOrDefault<T>(…) call sites removed from src/
RtServiceProvider class deleted (or kept only if it has remaining non-Get callers, e.g. the AsyncLocal Use scope; document the remaining surface in that case)

New architecture gate NoRtServiceProviderInProduction added under tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Architecture/, mirroring NoConcreteWorkspaceLoaderInProduction; flags any production reference to RtServiceProvider.Get or .GetOrDefault outside the class declaration itself
rt dump-help startup succeeds, every command listed, every Info.Examples invocation still works end-to-end (dogfood smoke matrix)
All existing tests pass; mutation tests that previously relied on WorkspaceLoader.UseOverride continue to pass via the same AsyncLocal hook
dotnet build, dotnet format --verify-no-changes, and the full test suite all clean
userStories.resolution: Completed on branch us-072-ctor-injection (PR forthcoming). IRtCommand.Build() is now an instance member; all ~50 commands under src/RoslynTools.Cli/Commands/ migrated to constructor-injected services (commits 199eefe through e1560db). RtServiceProvider.cs deleted entirely — Get/GetOrDefault eliminated and Use no longer needed because no consumers remain. Three production services (FixNamespaceService, ExtractClassService, ConsoleLoggingCore) also migrated. Bootstrap.cs registers ILogger<> via RtConsoleLogger<> as an open generic so Scrutor-discovered services with ILogger<T> ctor params resolve cleanly. Tests retrofitted to xUnit IClassFixture<RtServicesFixture> and resolve commands/services via _services.Resolve<T>(). NoRtServiceProviderInProduction architecture gate unskipped and passing. Full suite green (1146 + 9 tests), dotnet format clean.
userStories.notes: P2. Follow-on from EP-008 (US-053/US-054). Scope: 64 RtServiceProvider.Get/GetOrDefault call sites across 46 files. Approach approved 2026-05-21: convert IRtCommand from static Build() factory to instance class so DI can ctor-inject services. App.Discover resolves each command via the service provider. RtServiceProvider class deleted (or shrunk to just the AsyncLocal Use scope if needed). New NoRtServiceProviderInProduction architecture gate mirrors NoConcreteWorkspaceLoaderInProduction. Trunk-based delivery.

userStories.title: rt analyze list-smells: add --top N limiter
userStories.description: As an agent driving rt, I want `rt analyze list-smells --top N` to cap the output to the N highest-priority smells so that I can run concise smell scans without paging through thousands of lines of JSON.
acceptanceCriteria: rt analyze list-smells --solution <sln> --top 30 exits 0 and emits at most 30 smell entries to stdout
Ordering is deterministic and matches the existing default ordering (highest severity/score first; tie-break by file path then line)
Omitting --top preserves current behaviour (no limit)
--top 0 emits an empty smells array (still valid JSON with metadata intact)
--top with a negative integer exits 1 with stderr 'Invalid --top value: must be >= 0' (no stack trace)
rt dump-help shows --top in the list-smells command help
ListSmellsCommand.Info.Examples includes a --top example
userStories.notes: P2. Source: FB-006 (feedback.json, 2026-05-15). Pure CLI surface — slice the result list after ranking, before JSON serialisation. No behavioural change to the analyser itself.

userStories.title: make rt parallel-safe for agent dogfooding (feedback file, wrapper rebuild, deploy-skill, MSBuild obj)
userStories.description: As an agent running /execute-style parallel rt invocations across worktrees, I want rt and its build/deploy plumbing to be safe under concurrency so that parallel dogfooding does not corrupt feedback.json, race the rt.cmd rebuild, fight deploy-skill Copy-Item, or trip MSBuild obj/Debug file locks.
acceptanceCriteria: rt feedback add is safe under concurrent invocation: parallel calls each get a unique FB-id and every entry is persisted (regression test runs N parallel `rt feedback add` and asserts N distinct ids + N items on disk)

Concurrent ./rt.cmd / rt.ps1 invocations after a source edit serialise on a build mutex so only one rebuild runs at a time; subsequent invocations wait then execute against the freshly built binary (no CS2012 / rt.exe copy-lock warnings)
deploy-skill Copy-Item retries on file-lock with bounded backoff, or skips with a clear stderr message when the destination is locked by a concurrent build (no unhandled IOException)

Read-only `rt analyze …` commands accept a flag (e.g. --isolated-obj) or unconditionally redirect BaseIntermediateOutputPath to a per-process temp dir so parallel analyses do not race on shared obj/Debug files
Integration test exercises FB-007/FB-008/FB-013 reproduction scenarios in parallel and confirms no exceptions and no MSBuild lock warnings on stderr
Documentation update in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md noting that rt is now parallel-safe for agent use
userStories.notes: P2. Source cluster: FB-007, FB-008, FB-012, FB-013 (feedback.json, 2026-05-15). Four distinct race sites but one story — each is a small fix and they share the same trigger (parallel agent invocation). Implementation order: (1) feedback file mutex (FileStream with FileShare.None + retry loop on id allocation), (2) rt.cmd build mutex via named mutex around dotnet build, (3) deploy-skill retry, (4) MSBuildWorkspace BaseIntermediateOutputPath isolation for read-only commands.

userStories.title: stop capturing handled user-error exceptions to feedback.json
userStories.description: As a roslyn-tools maintainer, I want App.CaptureExceptionAsync to skip exception types that App.TryHandleUserErrorAsync already maps to a clean exit-1 + stderr UX, so feedback.json only collects genuinely unexpected failures that need human triage — not the expected bad-input UX paths that the dogfood/integration harness exercises on every run.
acceptanceCriteria: App.TryHandleUserErrorAsync (src/RoslynTools.Cli/App.cs:342) no longer calls CaptureExceptionAsync for exception types it already translates (FileNotFoundException, IOException, InvalidOperationException, JsonException, YamlException) — those are documented, expected user errors with a clean stderr message and exit 1; capturing them adds noise without adding signal
Exceptions that fall through TryHandleUserErrorAsync (return false → rethrow) ARE still captured to feedback.json — the unmapped path is the one that needs human triage

Running the bad-input integration scenarios (`refactor add-xml-doc --from-json <invalid.json>`, `inspect describe Foo --decisions <invalid.yaml>`, `inspect describe Foo --solution <missing.slnx>`, `analyze analyze-interface <non-interface>`) leaves feedback.json untouched — exit code is still 1, stderr is still the friendly message, but no FB-NNN entry is appended
Regression test added under tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Cli/ that runs one of the four scenarios end-to-end and asserts feedback.json count is unchanged
Existing tests pass; dotnet format --verify-no-changes clean
userStories.notes: P3. Source cluster: FB-280 through FB-299 (feedback.json, 2026-05-22) — 5 repeated runs of 4 identical scenarios from a dogfood/integration harness that exercises bad-input UX paths. All four scenarios are already handled correctly by TryHandleUserErrorAsync (exit 1 + stderr); the only output of those captures was 20 lines of feedback.json noise. Implementation: invert the order in TryHandleUserErrorAsync — only capture when the exception is NOT in the handled set (i.e. capture inside the trailing `return false` branch, not at the top). The 20 FB-280..FB-299 entries themselves are discarded; this story will be the audit trail.

userStories.title: rt <command> --help: show the same rich content as `rt dump-help` for that command
userStories.description: As an agent or developer running `rt <cmd> --help` (or `rt <group> <cmd> --help`), I want the same rich content that `rt dump-help` emits for that command — the `WhenToUse` description, the full `Examples` list, the supported output formats — instead of System.CommandLine's default option-listing. The richer help only lives in `RtCommandInfo` today, surfaced via `dump-help`; per-command `--help` shows only the option list. That forces every consumer to run `rt dump-help | grep` (or load the use-rt skill) to learn how to invoke a command.
acceptanceCriteria: Running `rt inspect describe --help` prints (in order): the command description, the `WhenToUse` paragraph, the Examples list (one fenced bash block, same format dump-help uses), the supported output formats, the aliases, the options, and the known-issues block when non-empty
Running `rt describe --help` (root shortcut) produces the same output — both invocation paths share one help renderer
Running `rt inspect --help` (group level) lists every command in the group with one-line descriptions plus aliases (same shape dump-help uses for the group section)
Running `rt --help` (root) lists groups and the unqualified command shortcuts, matching dump-help's contents table

The rendering uses the same `DumpHelpCommand` helpers wherever possible (RenderColouredCommandHeader, RenderColouredGroup) so the two outputs stay in lockstep — no duplicate format strings to maintain
ANSI colour is honoured when the destination is a TTY; plain text is emitted when piped (existing rt rule)
All 52 commands' `--help` output renders without exception; smoke test (`for each command: dotnet run ... -- <cmd> --help` exits 0)

Snapshot tests under tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Cli/ pin the help output for at least three representative commands (one inspect, one analyze, one refactor) so a future change to RtCommandInfo or the renderer is caught
Documentation: CLAUDE.md mention that `--help` shows the same content as `rt dump-help <command>` so agents can stop scraping dump-help output
userStories.notes: P2. Source: 2026-05-22 user request — 'add a task to add detailed help on any command. this should be the same thing we get from dump-help'. The hard work is already done: RtCommandInfo (WhenToUse, Examples, KnownIssues, SupportedFormats) is populated for every command and DumpHelpCommand already renders it. App.GetHelpLayout at App.cs:299 already partially intercepts the help layout for commands (RenderColouredCommandHeader) — extend that path to also inject the examples + known-issues sections, and add a fallback for the root + group cases.
